source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Carrollton campus is one of only 19 Texas data centers that publish a power figure, and at 45 MW it is the state's third largest disclosed site.

The 45 MW of IT load across 600,000 square feet works out to about 1,100 racks at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density. That is the physical constraint that matters: the building's power feed and floor space set a ceiling on how many accelerators can run there, and no amount of capital or chip supply raises it. The reading's estimate of 4,400 to 8,800 H100-equivalent accelerators is a range, not a measurement, because the operator does not publish rack counts or actual utilization.

Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities, but only 19 disclose power. The 45 MW here is 9.5 percent of the state's 475 MW of published IT load, which means the disclosed total is a floor, not a picture of Texas data center capacity. Most of the state's power draw is invisible in this data, so any conclusion about Texas as an AI hub rests on a small and possibly unrepresentative sample.

The certifications, PCI DSS, HIPAA, FISMA, ISO 27001, SSAE 16 Type II, and TIA-942, qualify the site for regulated workloads in payments, healthcare, and federal systems. None is specific to AI, and the operator does not say who the tenants are. The data covers one campus's published specifications and its rank within disclosed Texas capacity. It does not cover actual occupancy, contracted power, expansion plans, or whether any AI training happens there at all.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
